title: Operator Attestation & Network Handover PRD (sketch)
content:
Context:
This is a working PRD sketch for operator attestation, onboarding checks, and the networking handover flow for customer-managed private deployments (VPC/on-prem). Goal is to capture minimal viable gating (safety + auditability) so infra and SRE can run operator-level tasks inside customer environments with clear audit records and a safe roll-back path.

Why now:
- Increasing number of Private customers are requesting deeper operator access for initial provisioning and emergency troubleshooting.
- Legal/compliance teams want a short, auditable trail for operator actions and automated approval gates for network changes.
- We need a lightweight productized flow so Solutions and Professional Services don't have to run ad-hoc spreadsheets and Slack approvals.

Problem statement:
Many current handovers are ad-hoc: tickets, Slack approvals, emailed configs. There is no consistent attestation of who did what, limited ability to replay network-change sequences, and no standardized guardrails to prevent accidental exposure of customer VPCs or keys. This increases risk and slows down onboarding.

Objectives (MVP):
- Define a repeatable operator attestation flow that records: operator identity, justification, scope (time-limited role/session), and outcome.
- Implement approval gates for network-level actions (e.g., route table changes, peering, firewall rules). Approval can be: auto-approve for low-risk ops, single approver for medium-risk, multi-approver for high-risk.
- Produce a standardized audit log schema (events + metadata) that can be exported to customer SIEM and our control plane for retention and search.
- Create a handover checklist / operator-runbook template used by Solutions/PS during onboarding.

Non-goals (MVP exclusions):
- Full RBAC UI in Console for customer-managed operator sessions (can be a follow-up).
- Deep integration with all customer KMS/HSM variants (we will rely on existing KMS connectors and document gaps).

Key success metrics:
- 90% of new Private deployments use the standard handover checklist by Q2 after launch.
- Reduction in emergency escalation time by 40% (measured by mean time to resolve onboarding issues).
- Audit events for operator actions ingested successfully into control plane in 95% of handovers.

High-level UX flow (sketch):
1) Kickoff: Solutions opens a "Handover Session" via Console or a lightweight web-flow. Fill in customer, scope, requested ops, planned window.
2) Pre-checks: automated validations (VPC reachability, expected subnets, baseline firewall rules). If validation fails, session is blocked until resolved.
3) Approval gate: risk scoring determines required approvers. Approvers are notified with a one-click approve/deny and optional comments.
4) Operator session: upon approval, ephemeral credentials (time-limited, scope-limited) are issued. All operator activity is recorded locally (agent) and streamed to control plane as signed audit events.
5) Post-check & close: automated sanity checks (connectivity, ACLs) run; session owner tags as complete; retention policy applied to audit records.

Approval gate rules (initial proposals):
- Low risk: metadata-only changes, tagging, non-route security group updates -> auto-approve with 24h retrospective alert.
- Medium risk: firewall port openings, NAT modifications -> single approver (team lead or SRE oncall).
- High risk: VPC peering, route table additions to customer-managed peers, cross-account IAM role creation -> two approvers including security or customer contact.

Audit log schema (MVP fields):
- timestamp (ISO8601)
- event_id (uuid)
- session_id (uuid)
- operator_name (email)
- operator_role (e.g., solutions-engineer)
- action_type (enum: CREATE_ROUTE, MODIFY_SG, ISSUE_TEMP_CREDENTIALS, RUN_SCRIPT, etc.)
- target_resource (ARN/IP/CIDR/description)
- request_payload (string - sanitized)
- response_status (SUCCESS|FAIL|WARN)
- justification (free text short)
- approver_ids (list as CSV string)
- approval_decision (APPROVED|DENIED|AUTO_APPROVED)
- source_agent_version (e.g., v0.5.2)
- signature (base64) - operator-signed hash to ensure tamper-evidence

Retention & export:
- Default retention: 1 year in Redwood control plane for Private customers, configurable up to customer policy (30d, 90d, 365d).
- Export formats: syslog stream, S3 dump (encrypted), direct SIEM webhook.

Operator agent behavior (notes):
- Agent runs in customer environment (customer-managed). It buffers events locally and streams them to Redwood control plane via TLS with mTLS client certs created during onboarding.
- If network is offline, agent persists signed events to local disk with strict encrypt+WORM semantics until upload succeeds.
- Agent must perform minimal exfil prevention: block arbitrary attachments; redact environment variables from executed shells; provide explicit opt-in for debug captures.

Handover checklist (starter template):
- Customer ready: network diagram + CIDR map uploaded?
- IAM service account created for Redwood operator? (list ARN)
- KMS key accessible for logs? (yes/no)
- Onboarding window scheduled and customer POC on call?
- Agent version agreed and install method approved (helm/tar)?
- BCP/rollback plan uploaded?
- Approver list defined and contactable?

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Console UI: create/track Handover Session and display current status and approvers.
- Approval system: supports auto/single/multi approver flows and emits decision events into audit log.
- Agent: emits signed audit events according to schema, handles offline buffering and uploads within 24h when connectivity restored.
- Export: one customer test shows logs arriving in customer SIEM via webhook.

Open questions / risks (TODOs):
- Signature model: use operator-signed HMAC with per-session key or a PKI signature? Tradeoffs: PKI gives stronger non-repudiation but is heavier to manage.
- Reputational risk if operator session is abused: do we require customer explicit consent per session? (Legal leaning towards explicit consent).
- Data residency: some customers require logs to never leave their VPC. For those, we need a pattern to push logs to customer S3 or webhook instead of storing in our control plane.
- Audit log volume & cost: need cost model for storing signed events long-term; recommend chunking + compressing payloads.

Implementation notes / next steps:
- Engineering spike: prototype agent signed event envelope and offline buffering (owner: Mateo, ETA: 3 weeks).
- Product: design minimal Handover session UI and approval rules config (owner: Priya, ETA: 2 weeks).
- Security: recommend threat model review and KMS integration doc (owner: Emily, ETA: 1 week).
- Solutions/PS: pilot with two customers, collect feedback on checklist and approval friction (owner: Claire, ETA: 6 weeks).

Appendix: example event (human-readable)
- [2026-02-14T15:23:10Z] EVENT 3f2e... SESSION s-19b: operator=aaron.koh@redwood.com ACTION=CREATE_ROUTE TARGET=10.12.0.0/16 via igw-09fd RESPONSE=SUCCESS JUSTIFICATION=\"enable egress for inference cluster\" APPROVED_BY=emily.chen@redwood.com SIGNATURE=base64(... )

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally a sketch: looking for feedback on approval thresholds, signature model, retention policy, and whether we should require customer-side explicit approval per session.
- Please add links to any existing legal/compliance templates or customer contracts that mandate audit retention limits.

End of sketch.
